{"draft": "Airbnb revenue rises 17% in second quarter as bookings accelerate
Airbnb said second-quarter revenue advanced 17% year-over-year to $3.6 billion, with growth of 13% on an ex-FX basis, as demand lifted bookings across its regions.
The company reported gross booking value of $27.2 billion, up 16%, while nights and seats booked climbed 10% to 148.3 million. Its average daily rate was $184, up 5% from a year earlier, and its implied take rate was 13.2%.
Net income was $816 million, for a net income margin of 23%. Adjusted EBITDA grew 21% to $1.3 billion, and the adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 35%.
The company said app bookings remained a driver, with nights booked on its app increasing 23% and accounting for 64% of total nights booked. First-time bookers grew 11%, and bedroom nights booked rose over 12%.
Free cash flow was $1.3 billion, up 30%, with a 35% margin, while trailing twelve month free cash flow reached $4.8 billion at a 37% margin. The company repurchased $1.1 billion of Class A common stock during the quarter and held $12.1 billion of cash and cash equivalents, short-term investments, and restricted cash as of June 30, 2026.
For the third quarter, the company expects revenue of $4.69 billion to $4.77 billion, representing year-over-year growth of 15% to 17%. For full-year 2026, it now expects revenue growth to improve to at least mid teens and a full-year adjusted EBITDA margin of at least 35.5%."}
